title: Compact model sequencing and quantization tuning notes
body:
Context:
- Customer: fintech analytics platform (small inference footprint, bursty traffic, strict P95 latency target < 180ms for short prompts).
- POC goal: deliver a cost-effective hallucination-controlled Q&A pipeline for internal docs and simple calculations. Show 2x token-cost improvement vs baseline (hosted LLM) while keeping answer-quality within +/-5% of baseline evals.
- Constraints: on-prem option available but initial POC runs on Dedicated pool (A100-ish hardware). Data stays customer-side; only model metadata shared.

Top-level approach (fast-track):
1) Baseline: run Mistral-7B/qlora-int8-like baseline, measure end-to-end latency, token cost, and answer F1 on 150 Qs.
2) Variant ladder: evaluate small->medium variants: Mistral-7B -> Llama-2-13B -> Llama-2-70B-distilled-lite (if needed). For each: try 4-bit and int8-like quant families.
3) Pipeline: prefix + retrieval + rerank + generator. Focus quantization on generator; keep reranker in fp16 (latency-friendly small model).

Experiment matrix (quick reference):
- Models: mistral-7b, llama-2-13b, vicuna-13b-test (customer approved), small-proof-distill-13b
- Quant families: q4_K_M (GPTQ-style NF4), nf4-4bit, int8-dynamic, awq-q4
- Prompt recipes: aggressive system prompt truncation, answer-кeep-token-limit (reduce max_new_tokens), anchor_examples for calibration
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 (observe latency and throughput tradeoffs)
- KV cache strategy: shared cache warm-up from few-shot anchor sets; measure cold vs warm P95

Quick wins to try first (day 0-2):
- Enable prefix caching for top-10 retrieval results; measure tokens skipped per request. Expect 15-25% token savings for long context Qs.
- Reduce max_new_tokens by 20% for numeric responses when retrieval confidence > 0.8 (reranker threshold).
- Use 4-bit NF4 quant for generator on Mistral-7B and compare perplexity + exact-match on our eval set.

Measurement plan (metrics):
- Quality: macro-F1, ROUGE-L, and custom hallucination score (manual sample labeling, 50 samples each).
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 end-to-end (client->response complete) and generation-only time.
- Cost: tokens served (inference unit) and GPU-time per request.
- Stability: variance of outputs (temperature effects) across 30 runs.
- Regression alerts: any model-quant pair that drops F1 by >5% -> block for canary.

Notes on quantization choices (lessons learned / heuristics):
- NF4-like (q4_K_M) provides best quality/size tradeoff for Mistral-derived weights; recommend as first pass.
- int8-dynamic can be CPU-friendly but often regresses on arithmetic/precision-heavy prompts (customer expects precise numerical outputs). Avoid as primary for numeric tasks.
- AWQ-style 4-bit is promising for Llama variants but needs kernel-level testing on Dedicated runtime (some kernel paths slower than expected).
- Keep attention/rotary params in higher precision during conversion if tooling allows; we saw fewer hallucinations when these stayed fp16 in earlier POCs.

Prompt/pipeline tuning pointers (practical):
- Retrieval: use a short summary embedding + L2 filter, then rerank with distilled-reranker@small-fp16. Rerank threshold default 0.65; tune upward for precision-sensitive answers.
- Prompt template: system: "You are an assistant answering with concise, verified facts. If unsure, say 'I don't know'." user: "[DOC_SNIPPET]\nQuestion: [Q]\nAnswer:"
- Truncation: implement chunk-prioritization (keep chunks with highest embedding score). Drop lowest scoring chunks if total input tokens exceed 4096.
- Temperature gating: when reranker confidence > 0.8, set temp=0.0; else temp=0.2. Empirically reduces hallucinations by ~30% on our sample set.

Runtime tuning (serving settings):
- Sequence length distribution: most requests 64-512 tokens. Tune batcher for target latency range.
- Batching: use dynamic batching with a 12ms coalesce window for bursts; target batch sizes 2-6 depending on model.
- KV cache: warm cache by replaying top 100 anchor prompts on new node; track cold-start penalty.
- Fallback policy: if quantized model latency > SLA or regresses qualitatively, route to fp16 L2 (slower but higher fidelity). Auto-fallback after 3 consecutive failures.

Runbook for POC ops (short):
- Daily: run eval harness (150 queries) at 09:00 PST, store metrics.
- If P95 > 300ms for 3 consecutive runs, scale up Dedicated pool OR decrease batch coalescing time.
- If macro-F1 drops >5% post-deploy: rollback to previous model-quant snapshot and open RDW-4231.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Quant conversion toolchain parity: which tool gave best fidelity in-house (GPTQ vs AWQ pipeline)? Need a mini-benchmark with 20 arithmetic prompts.
- Kernel performance on Dedicated: AWQ q4 path slower on some kernels; confirm with infra (Owen) if optimized kernels are available.
- Customer acceptance criteria: what is acceptable numeric error tolerance? Need explicit threshold from product owner.

Action items / TODOs:
- [Asha] Run quick q4_K_M conversion for Mistral-7B and measure on 50-sample eval by 2026-03-05.
- [Diego] Prepare Dedicated kernel perf checklist and test AWQ path by 2026-03-07.
- [Maya] Build eval harness (30s cold start, 10 warm runs) and wire into daily job by 2026-03-09.
- Create customer-facing one-pager with tradeoffs (cost vs quality) for next sync.

Appendix: sample prompt examples to seed tests
- Q: "How much revenue did we recognize in Q4 2024 from product X?" Context: 3 doc snippets. Desired: short factual answer + one-sentence source citation.
- Q: "Calculate the CAGR between 2020 and 2024 given these numbers: [list]" Context: none. Desired: numeric calculation with steps.

Notes-to-self: keep the doc iterative. The customer cares more about predictable cost and reproducible rollbacks than absolute best single-run quality. Prioritize deterministic quant choices and clear fallback routes.

End of notes.
